questions.question: A invests Rs. 6,00,000 more than B in a business. B invests his capital for \(7\frac{1}{2}\) months, while A invests his capital for \(2\frac{1}{2}\) more months than B. Out of the total profit of Rs. 12,40,000, if the share of B is Rs. 2,48,000 less than the share of A, then the capital of B is:
questions.questionHtml: A invests Rs. 6,00,000 more than B in a business. B invests his capital for \(7\frac{1}{2}\) months, while A invests his capital for \(2\frac{1}{2}\) more months than B. Out of the total profit of Rs. 12,40,000, if the share of B is Rs. 2,48,000 less than the share of A, then the capital of B is:
questions.solution:
Concept used:

Profit = Investment × Time

Calculation:

Total profit = 12,40,000

Let profit of A be x

Profit of B = x – 248000

x + x – 2,48,000 = 12,40,000

2x = 12,40,000 + 2,48,000

2x = 1488000

x = 744000

Profit of A = 744000

Profit of B = 744000 – 248000 = 496000

Let money invested by B be Rs y.

Money invested by A = y + 600000

Time for B = \(7\frac{1}{2} = \frac{{15}}{2}\;months\)

Time for A = \(7\frac{1}{2} + 2\frac{1}{2} = 10\;months\)

As we know,

Capital × Time = Profit

(y + 6,00,000) × 10 : y × (15/2) = 744000 : 496000

10 (y + 6,00,000) : 15y/2 = 3 : 2

4 (y + 6,00,000) : 3y = 3 : 2

(4y + 24,00,000)/3y = 3/2

8y + 48,00,000 = 9y

9y – 8y = 48,00,000

y = 48,00,000

Shortcut Trick

As we know,

Capital × Time = Profit

Profit share of A to B = 3 : 2

Time ratio of A to B = 10 : 15/2 = 4 : 3

According to the question

4A/3B = 3/2

A/B = 9/8

So, capital ratio of A to B = 9 : 8

(9 – 8) = 1 unit = 6,00,000

8 unit = 6,00,000 × 8 = 48,00,000

questions.question: Person A started a business by investing Rs. 65,000. After a few months, B joined him by investing Rs. 50,000. Three months after the joining of B, C joined the two with an investment of Rs. 55,000. At the end of the year, A got 50% of profit as his share. For how many months did A alone finance the business?
questions.questionHtml: Person A started a business by investing Rs. 65,000. After a few months, B joined him by investing Rs. 50,000. Three months after the joining of B, C joined the two with an investment of Rs. 55,000. At the end of the year, A got 50% of profit as his share. For how many months did A alone finance the business?
questions.solution:
Let, B invest the amount after x months, then  A , B and C invested for 12 months, (12 - x) months and (9 - x) months respectively

Profit share = 65,000 × 12 : 50,000 × (12 - x) : 55,000 × (9 - x) ⇒ 156 : 10(12 - x) : 11(9 - x)

A got 50% of profit as his share ⇒ 156/(156 + 120 - 10x + 99 - 11x) = 1/2 ⇒ 312 = 375 - 21x ⇒ x = 3 month

questions.question: A, B and C invested ₹40,000, ₹48,000 and ₹80,000, respectively, for a business at the start of a year. After six months, for the remaining time of the year, A added ₹4,000, B added ₹4,000 while C withdrew ₹4,000 every month. If the total profit is ₹6,72,000, then what is C's share (in ₹)?
questions.questionHtml: A, B and C invested ₹40,000, ₹48,000 and ₹80,000, respectively, for a business at the start of a year. After six months, for the remaining time of the year, A added ₹4,000, B added ₹4,000 while C withdrew ₹4,000 every month. If the total profit is ₹6,72,000, then what is C's share (in ₹)?
questions.solution:
After six months, for the remaining time of the year, (4000 × 6) + (4000 × 5) + (4000 × 4) + (4000 × 3) + (4000 × 2) + (4000 × 1) = 4000 × 21 = 84000

Now, profit will be distributed in the ratio,

A : B : C = [(40000 × 12) + 84000] : [(48000 × 12) + 84000] : [(80000 × 12) - 84000] ⇒ (480000 + 84000) : (576000 + 84000) : (960000 - 84000) ⇒ 564 : 660 : 876

The share of C ⇒ [876/(564 + 660 + 876)] × 672000 ⇒ (876/2100) × 672000 = 280320

questions.question: A started a business with a capital of Rs. 1,12,000. After 2 months, B joined the business with a capital of Rs, 80,000, and after another 2 months, C joined the business with a capital of Rs. 72,000. After 10 months from the start of the business, B withdrew Rs. 8,000 and C also withdrew Rs. 8,000. If B received Rs. 9,800 as his share in the profit at the end of a year, then the total profit was:
questions.questionHtml: A started a business with a capital of Rs. 1,12,000. After 2 months, B joined the business with a capital of Rs, 80,000, and after another 2 months, C joined the business with a capital of Rs. 72,000. After 10 months from the start of the business, B withdrew Rs. 8,000 and C also withdrew Rs. 8,000. If B received Rs. 9,800 as his share in the profit at the end of a year, then the total profit was:
questions.solution:
Given:-

A invests 1,12,000

B invests 80,000

C invests 72,000

Formula used:-

Capital × Time = Profit

Calculation:-

Total capital of A at the end of the year = 112,000 × 12 = 13,44,000

Total capital of B at the end of the year = 80,000 × 8 + 72,000 × 2 = 6,40,000 + 1,44,000

= 7,84,000

Total capital of C at the end of the year = 72000 × 6 + 64000 × 2 = 432000 + 128000 = 560000

Profit ratio of A, B and C = 1344000 : 784000 : 560000 = 84 : 49 : 35

49x = 9800

x = 9800/49 = 200

Total Profit = (84x + 49x + 35x) = 168x = 168 × 200 = Rs. 33600

Alternate Method

See, 112000 : 80000 : 72000 : 8000 : 8000

We can write this,

14 : 10 : 9 : 1 : 1

Now,

Capital of A = 14

Capital of B = 10

Capital of C = 9

Total capital at the end of the year = 14 × 12 = 168

Total capital of B at the end of the year = 10 × 8 + 9 × 2 = 80 + 18 = 98

Total capital of C at the end of the year = 9 × 6 + 8 × 2 = 54 + 16 = 70

Profit share of A, B and C = 168 : 98 : 70

98 unit = 9800

1 unit = 100

Total profit = 168 + 98 + 70 = 336

336 unit = 336 × 100 = Rs. 33600

questions.question: A and B had a joint business in which A invested Rs. 60,000 in the business for one year. After 3 months B invested Rs. 80,000. At the beginning of the second year, A invested Rs. 30,000 more and B withdrew Rs. 5,000. At the end of two years, profit earned by A is Rs. 35,880. What is the profit (in Rs.) earned by B, if they distributed half of the total profit equally and rest in the capital ratio?
questions.questionHtml: A and B had a joint business in which A invested Rs. 60,000 in the business for one year. After 3 months B invested Rs. 80,000. At the beginning of the second year, A invested Rs. 30,000 more and B withdrew Rs. 5,000. At the end of two years, profit earned by A is Rs. 35,880. What is the profit (in Rs.) earned by B, if they distributed half of the total profit equally and rest in the capital ratio?
questions.solution:
Profit will be distributed in the ratio, A : B ⇒ ( 60,000 × 12 + 90,000 × 12) : (80,000 × 9 + 75,000 × 12) ⇒ 1,800,000 : 1,620,000 ⇒ 10 : 9

Here, out of 4p profit, 2p is equally divided between A and B.

A's profit ⇒ p + \(10 \over 19\) × 2p = 35,880 ⇒ p = 35,880 × \(19\over 39\) = Rs 17,480

Now,Profit earned by B = p + \(9 \over 19\) × 2p  ⇒ \(37p\over 19\) = \(37\over 19\) × 17,480 ⇒ Rs 34,040.

questions.question: A, B and C started a business with their capitals in the ratio 1 : 4 : 4. At the end of every 3 months, A doubles his capital, B halves his capital and C leaves his capital unchanged. At the end of the year, if B’s share in the profit was Rs. 4,50,000, then the total profit (in Rs. Lakhs) was ______.
questions.questionHtml: A, B and C started a business with their capitals in the ratio 1 : 4 : 4. At the end of every 3 months, A doubles his capital, B halves his capital and C leaves his capital unchanged. At the end of the year, if B’s share in the profit was Rs. 4,50,000, then the total profit (in Rs. Lakhs) was ______.
questions.solution:
As we know,

Capital × time = Profit

Capital ratio of A, B and C = 1 : 4 : 4

Capital of A at the end of the year = (1 + 2 + 4 + 8) × 3 = 15 × 3

Capital of B at the end of the year = (4 + 2 + 1 + 0.5) × 3 = 7.5 × 3

Capital of C at the end of the year = (4 + 4 + 4 + 4) × 3 = 16 × 3

Capital of A, B and C at the end of the year = 15 : 7.5 : 16

7.5 unit = 4,50,000

1 unit = 4,50,000/7.5 = 60000

(15 + 7.5 + 16 = 38.5) unit = 60000 × 38.5 = 2310000 = 23.1 lakhs

questions.question: A, B and C are partners in a business. A, whose capital has been used for 5 months, claims 1/7 of the profit. B whose capital has been used for 7 months, claims 1/5 of the profit. C has invested Rs. 4,600 for 9 months. How much capital did A contribute?
questions.questionHtml: A, B and C are partners in a business. A, whose capital has been used for 5 months, claims 1/7 of the profit. B whose capital has been used for 7 months, claims 1/5 of the profit. C has invested Rs. 4,600 for 9 months. How much capital did A contribute?
questions.solution:
Given:

A capital usage = 5 months

B capital usage = 7 months

C capital = Rs, 4600

A profit = 1/7

B profit = 1/5

C time = 9 months

Formula used:

Capital × Time = Profit

Calculation:

Let the total profit be 35 unit.

Profit of A = 1/7 × 35 = 5 unit

Profit of B = 1/5 × 35 = 7 unit

Profit of C = 35 – 5 – 7 = 23 unit

Let the capital of A and B are x and y, respectively.

As we know,

Capital × Time = Profit

⇒ 5x : 7y ∶ 4600 × 9 = 5 : 7 : 23

According to the question

⇒ 23 unit = 4600 × 9

⇒ 1 unit = (4600 × 9)/23

⇒ 5 unit = 5x

⇒ [(4600 × 9)/23] × 5 = 5x

⇒ x = [(4600 × 9)/23] × 5/5 = 1800

∴The correct answer is Rs.1800.

questions.question: A man started off a business with a certain capital amount. In the first year, he earned 60% profit and donated 50% of the total capital (initial amount + profit). He followed the same procedure with the remaining capital after the second and the third year. If at the end of the three years, he is left with Rs. 15,360, what was the initial amount (in Rs.) with which the man started his business?
questions.questionHtml: A man started off a business with a certain capital amount. In the first year, he earned 60% profit and donated 50% of the total capital (initial amount + profit). He followed the same procedure with the remaining capital after the second and the third year. If at the end of the three years, he is left with Rs. 15,360, what was the initial amount (in Rs.) with which the man started his business?
questions.solution:
Let the captial at the starting be 100a

After 1st year, his capital = 100a + 100a × 60% ⇒ 160a, and after donating, his capital = 160a - 160a × 50% ⇒ 80a

After 2nd year, his capital = 80a + 80a × 60% ⇒ 128a, and after donating, his capital = 128a - 128a × 50% ⇒ 64a

After 3rd year, his capital = 64a + 64a × 60% ⇒ 102.4a, and after donating, his capital = 102.4a - 102.4a × 50% ⇒ 51.2a

Here, in the question ⇒ 51.2a = Rs. 15360 ⇒ a = 300

So, his capital at the starting ⇒ 100a = 300 × 100 = Rs. 30000

questions.question: Keshav, Surjeet and Thomas started a business with investments in the ratio 2 ∶ 3 ∶ 4. The ratio of their period of investments is 5 ∶ 6 ∶ 9. Twenty percent of the profit was spent on rent and maintenance of the office. Remaining profit was distributed among themselves. If the difference in the shares of profit of Keshav and Surjeet is Rs.7264, then how much is the total profit (in Rs.)?
questions.questionHtml: Keshav, Surjeet and Thomas started a business with investments in the ratio 2 ∶ 3 ∶ 4. The ratio of their period of investments is 5 ∶ 6 ∶ 9. Twenty percent of the profit was spent on rent and maintenance of the office. Remaining profit was distributed among themselves. If the difference in the shares of profit of Keshav and Surjeet is Rs.7264, then how much is the total profit (in Rs.)?
questions.solution:
Given:

Ratio of investment of Keshav, Surjeet and Thomas = 2 : 3 : 4

The ratio of their period of investments = 5 : 6 : 9

Profit spent on rent and maintenance = 20%

The difference in the shares of profit of Keshav and Surjeet = Rs. 7264

Formula used:

Profit = Investment × Time

Calculation:

Let the ratio of their period of investments be 5x, 6x and 9x respectively

Profit of Keshav = (5x × 2) = 10x

Profit of Surjeet = (6x × 3) = 18x

Profit of Thomas = (9x × 4) = 36x

According to the question 

18x - 10x = 7264

⇒ x = 908

So, Profit of Keshav + Surjeet + Thomas = 64x 

⇒ 64 × 908 = 58112

But it is the 80% of the actual profit 

So, 80% is equivalent to 58112

So, 100% is equivalent to 58112 × 5/4 = 72640

∴ The required total profit is Rs. 72640

questions.questionHtml: Kapil initiated a business with an investment of ₹30,00,000 in April 2022. After six months, his friend Kunal joined him with an investment of ₹25,00,000. In February 2023, Kapil's Ex-Class fellow Saloni also invested an amount equal to the total investment made by the earlier two partners. questions.solution:
Kapil's money was invested for 36 months, Kunal's money was invested for 30 months

Saloni's money  (30,00,000 + 25,00,000) = 55,00,000  was invested for 26 months.

The profit ratio will be,

 30,00,000 × 36 : 25,00,000 × 30: 55,00,000 × 26 ⇒ 108 : 75 : 143

questions.question: A, B and C enter into a partnership by investing their capitals in the ratio of 2/5 : 3/4 : 5/8. After 4 months, A increased his capital by 50% but B decreased his capital by 20%. What is the share of B in the total profit of Rs. 2,82,100 at the end of a year?
questions.questionHtml: A, B and C enter into a partnership by investing their capitals in the ratio of 2/5 : 3/4 : 5/8. After 4 months, A increased his capital by 50% but B decreased his capital by 20%. What is the share of B in the total profit of Rs. 2,82,100 at the end of a year?
questions.solution:
Ratio of capitals invested by A, B and C = 2/5 : 3/4 : 5/8 = 16 : 30 : 25

Let capital of A, B and C are 16x, 30x and 25x respectively.

Capital of A at the end of the year = 16x × 4 + 24x × 8 = 64x + 192x = 256x

Capital of B at the end of the year = 30x × 4 + 24x × 8 = 120x + 192x = 312x

Capital of C at the end of the year = 25x × 12 = 300x

Capital ratio of A, B and C at the end of the year = 256x : 312x : 300x = 64x : 78x : 75x

According to the question

64x + 78x + 75x = 282100

217x = 282100

x = 282100/217 = 1300

Profit share of B at the end of the year = 78x = 78 × 1300 = 101400

At the end of every quarter, A halves his capital, Whereas B doubles his capital and C leaves his capital unchanged. If at the end of a year, A’s profit was Rs. 24,000, then what is the total profit (in Rs.)?
questions.solution:
Capital of A, B and C = 4 : 2 : 9

⇒ Suppose capital of A = 4

⇒ Suppose capital of B = 2

⇒ Suppose capital of C = 9

⇒ Total capital of A after end of the year = 4 × 3 + (4/2) × 3 + (4/4) × 3 + (4/8) × 3

= 12 + 6 + 3 + (3/2) = 45/2

⇒ Total capital of B after end of the year = 2 × 3 + 4 × 3 + 8 × 3 + 16 × 3 = 6 + 12 + 24 + 48

= 90

⇒ Total capital of C after end of the year = 9 × 12 = 108

⇒ Profit ratio of A, B and C = (45/2) : 90 : 108 = 5 : 20 : 24

⇒ 5 unit = 24000

⇒ 1 unit = 24000/5 = 4800

⇒ (5 + 20 + 24) unit = 49 unit = 4800 × 49 = Rs. 235200

⇒ Total profit = Rs. 235200

Profit Ratio = (InvestmentA × TimeA) : (InvestmentB × TimeB)

5 : 9 = (IA × 8) : (36,000 × 12)

IA = (5 ÷ 9) × (36,000 × 12 ÷ 8)

IA = 5 × 4,000 × 1.5 = 30,000

Share of C = 75 × 30 = Rs. 2250

questions.question: A, B and C started a business. A invested \(33\frac{1}{3}\%\) of the total capital, B invest \(33\frac{1}{3}\%\) of the remaining capital and C, the remaining. If the total profit, at the end of a year, was Rs. 20,250 then the profit of C exceeds the profit of B by:
questions.questionHtml: A, B and C started a business. A invested \(33\frac{1}{3}\%\) of the total capital, B invest \(33\frac{1}{3}\%\) of the remaining capital and C, the remaining. If the total profit, at the end of a year, was Rs. 20,250 then the profit of C exceeds the profit of B by:
questions.solution:
Given:

A invested \(33\frac{1}{3}\%\) of the total capital, B invested \(33\frac{1}{3}\%\) of the remaining capital and C, the remaining.

Total profit = Rs. 20250

Concept used:

The ratio of investment = Ratio of profit share.

Calculation:

Let total capital be 9x, then

Capital of A = 9x × 1/3 = 3x

Capital of B = (9x – 3x) × 1/3 = 2x

Capital of C = 6x – 2x = 4x

The profit share of A, B, and C at the end of the year = 3x : 2x : 4x

Total profit = 20250

3x + 2x + 4x = 20250

9x = 20250/9

x = 2250

The profit share of C is more than that of B by = (4x – 2x) × 2250 = 4500

Shortcut Trick Let total capital be 9.

\({33}{1\over3}\)% = \(1\over3\)

  A B C
  9 × \(1\over3\) = 3

9 - 3 = 6

6 × \(1\over3\) = 2

 6- 2 = 4
Ratio 3 2 4

So, (3 + 2 + 4) = Rs. 20,250

⇒ 9 → 20,250

⇒ 1 → 2,250

The profit share of C is more than that of B by

⇒ (4 - 2) × 2,250 = Rs. 4,500

questions.solution:
The invested capital by them be P, Q, and R respectively.

questions.question: Three partners shared the profit in a business in the ratio 8 : 7 : 5. They invested their capitals for 7 months, 8 months and 14 months, respectively. What was the ratio of their capitals?
questions.questionHtml: Three partners shared the profit in a business in the ratio 8 : 7 : 5. They invested their capitals for 7 months, 8 months and 14 months, respectively. What was the ratio of their capitals?
questions.solution:
Given:

Profit ratio of three partners = 8 : 7 : 5

Period of investment of 1st partner = 7 months

Period of investment of 2nd partner = 8 months

Period of investment of 3rd partner = 14 months

Concept used:

Person’s Profit = Investment × time period

Calculation:

Let the investment and time period be 7x : 8y : 14z

7x/8y = 8/7

⇒ 49x = 64y

⇒ y = 49x/64

7x/14z = 8/5

⇒ 35x = 112z

⇒ z = 35x/112

⇒ z = 5x/16

x : y : z = x : 49x/64 : 5x/16

⇒ Multiply by 64

x : y : z = 64 : 49 : 20

∴ The investment ratio is 64 : 49 : 20

Shortcut Trick We know that, 

⇒ Profit = Invested Capital × Invested Time 

Let the invested capital of all 3 be a, b, and c respectively, 

⇒ 

Now we get,

⇒ a × 7 = 8

⇒ a = 8/7

similarly, we get, b = 7/8 & c = 5/14

Now we have a = 8/7, b = 7/8,  and c = 5/14

Multiplying by 56, we get, 

⇒ 8/7(56), 7/8(56), and 5/14(56)

⇒ 64, 49, and 20

∴ The investment ratio is 64 : 49 : 20.

questions.question: A sum (in Rs.) is distributed between A, B and C in the ratio 9 : 6 : 11. If A gives Rs. 500 from his share to C, the ratio of shares of A, B and C becomes 4 : 3 : 6. What is the sum of shares (in Rs.) of B and C, in the beginning?
questions.questionHtml: A sum (in Rs.) is distributed between A, B and C in the ratio 9 : 6 : 11. If A gives Rs. 500 from his share to C, the ratio of shares of A, B and C becomes 4 : 3 : 6. What is the sum of shares (in Rs.) of B and C, in the beginning?
questions.solution:
Given:

A : B : C = 9 : 6 : 11

A gives Rs. 500

New ratio of A, B, C = 4 : 3 : 6

Calculation:

Sum of ratio of A, B and C = 9x : 6x : 11x

According to the question

⇒ (9x – 500)/(11x + 500) = 4/6 = 2/3

⇒ 3(9x – 500) = 2(11x + 500)

⇒ 27x – 1500 = 22x + 1000

⇒ 27x – 22x = 1000 + 1500

⇒ 5x = 2500

⇒ x = 500

Sum of share of B and C = 6x + 11x = 17x = 17 × 500 = 8500

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 8,500.

questions.question: Nikhil and Neha invested capital in the ratio 5 ∶ 4. The time Neha invested her money for was one year more than that invested by Nikhil. The ratio of their profits is in the ratio 6 ∶ 5. Find the time Neha invested the money for.
questions.questionHtml: Nikhil and Neha invested capital in the ratio 5 ∶ 4. The time Neha invested her money for was one year more than that invested by Nikhil. The ratio of their profits is in the ratio 6 ∶ 5. Find the time Neha invested the money for.
questions.solution:
The time invested by Nikhil be T, then time invested by Neha is (T+1) ⇒ 5T/4(T+1) = 6/5 ⇒ 25T = 24T + 24 ⇒ T = 24.

Neha invested the money for (T + 1) = 24 + 1 = 25 years.

questions.question: Three partners P, Q and R invest ₹1,000, ₹1,200 and ₹1,500, respectively, in a business. What should be the share of Q if the total profit is ₹666?
questions.questionHtml: Three partners P, Q and R invest ₹1,000, ₹1,200 and ₹1,500, respectively, in a business. What should be the share of Q if the total profit is ₹666?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of investments = 1000 : 1200 : 1500 = 10 : 12 : 15.

Since the time period is identical, profit is distributed in the ratio of their investments.

Share of Q = [12 ÷ (10 + 12 + 15)] × Total Profit

Share of Q = (12 ÷ 37) × 666 = 12 × 18 = 216.

∴ The correct answer is ₹216.

Alternate Method

Given:

Investment of P = ₹1000

Investment of Q = ₹1200

Investment of R = ₹1500

Total profit = ₹666

Formula Used:

When the investment time is the same for all partners, Profit Ratio = Capital Ratio.

Calculation:

⇒ Ratio of profits (P : Q : R) = 1000 : 1200 : 1500

⇒ Simplifying the ratio, we get 10 : 12 : 15

⇒ Sum of ratio parts = 10 + 12 + 15 = 37 parts

⇒ Value of 37 parts = ₹666

⇒ Value of 1 part = 666 ÷ 37 = ₹18

⇒ Profit share of Q = 12 parts

⇒ Share of Q = 12 × 18 = ₹216

∴ The correct answer is ₹216.

Additional Information

Different Time Periods

If partners invest for different durations, their profit is shared in the ratio of the product of their Capital and Time (C1 × T1 : C2 × T2).

Working & Sleeping Partners

A working partner receives a fixed salary or a specific percentage of the total profit for managing the business. The remaining profit is distributed among all partners according to their investment ratios.

Compound Partnership

When a partner withdraws or adds money during the year, their capital is broken into time segments. The equivalent capital is calculated as (Amount1 × Months1) + (Amount2 × Months2).

questions.question: Rs. 15,000 was invested by A and B together to start a small business. They got a profit of Rs. 2,000 at the end of the year. B took his profit share of Rs. 600. How much did A invest?
questions.questionHtml: Rs. 15,000 was invested by A and B together to start a small business. They got a profit of Rs. 2,000 at the end of the year. B took his profit share of Rs. 600. How much did A invest?
questions.solution:
Given∶

Total profit of A and B together at the end of year = Rs. 2000

Profit of B = Rs. 600

Calculation∶

Profit of A = 2000 – 600 = Rs. 1400

Ratio of profit of A and B = 1400 ∶ 600 = 7 ∶ 3

We know that ratio of profit is equal to the ratio of investment. Here time investment is same for both therefore ratio of profit is equal to the ratio of money investment.

∴ Ratio of money investment = 7 ∶ 3

Total ratio = 7 + 3 = 10

⇒ Money invested by A = 7/10 × 15000 = Rs. 10500

If time of investment is equal for A and B then, ratio of profit earned by A and B is same as the ratio of investment done.

⇒ 37 : 45

questions.question: P. Q and R are partners and invest in a business. P invests 1/5th of total investments and Q invests 1/4th of the total investments. What is the ratio of investments of P, Q and R respectively?
questions.questionHtml: P. Q and R are partners and invest in a business. P invests 1/5th of total investments and Q invests 1/4th of the total investments. What is the ratio of investments of P, Q and R respectively?
questions.solution:
Let the total investment be L.C.M of (4, 5) = 20

P invests 1/5th of the total investment = 20/5 = Rs. 4, Q invests 1/4th of the total investment = (1/4) × 20 = Rs. 5

R invests = Rs 20 - (Rs. 4 + Rs. 5) ⇒ Rs. 11

Thus ratio of the profit of P, Q and R respectively is 4 : 5 : 11.
